title: Computing in Statistics
weeklyTopics: Intro: Python basics (Hello World, Python as a calculator)
Control flow: if statements, for/while loops (break, continue, else), pass, functions and arguments
Data structures: lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries, looping techniques
OS interface, command line arguments, math module, regex pattern matching
NumPy: creating arrays, basic operations, indexing and slicing
NumPy: manipulating arrays, universal functions (ufuncs), sorting/searching
SciPy: optimization, root finding, special functions, statistical functions
Pandas: Series, DataFrame, Panel data structures
Pandas: reading/writing text, databases, and web APIs
HPC computing on UMich's flux cluster (SSH login, MToken)
Hadoop/MapReduce: building an inverted index over text corpora
workloadNotes: Lecture materials are entirely Jupyter/IPython notebooks (nbformat 3) building from core Python up through NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, databases/web APIs, and finally distributed computing (Hadoop on the flux HPC cluster); repo includes a homeworks folder but grading breakdown not found in-repo.
